newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile supermarket sales down in April - trade group.
newsitem.headline: Chile supermarket sales down in April - trade group.

text.p: Chilean supermarket sales fell 1.7 percent in real terms in April compared with the same month last year, the trade group ASACH said on Wednesday.
Sales in the first four months of the year rose 1.5 percent, showing the effects of Chile's tight monetary policies, ASACH said in a statement.
"The analysis of these figures shows that despite better performance in the economy, supermarkets are still being affected by the adjustment process begun in mid-1996," the statement said.

In April, sales of non-perishable items fell 0.9 percent, while meat sales rose 6.5 percent. Other perishables slipped one percent, while sales in the "various" category plunged 16.3 percent, the statement said.

The "various" category includes items not considered essential and which "can be replaced by products considered to be of prime necessity," said the statement. The decline in that category reflected weaker consumer purchasing power because of the adjustment in monetary supply, the statement said.

In the first four months of the year, sales of non-perishables rose 10.6 percent, meat sales climbed 7.8 percent and sales of other perishables rose 0.6 percent, while the "various" category showed a 20 percent drop.
